correctness.rationale: The 12-vertex formula reduces directional width for every t in [0,1/2] to twice the largest plus c times the middle absolute direction coordinate. Five elementary spherical-chamber integrals give exact moments, and differentiating their rational ratio yields a unique minimum because rational interval arithmetic certifies 0<E<D. Endpoint, equality and extrema directions are separately proved. Independently implemented vertex enumeration, sphere integration, and rational interval checks replay from the packaged code; samples are not treated as proofs.

value.rationale: Directional width stability is a natural intrinsic observable when comparing orientation sensitivity of a canonical continuous family of equal-edge truncations. The complete exact two-moment profile yields a unique optimizer strictly between the tetrahedron and Archimedean truncation, not deducible from endpoint data; the separate directional-minimum orientation transition gives geometric context. It is a sharp classification of a motivated shape continuum rather than a parameterless elementary special case.
